chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Dawood, from Hammad, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the people of Makkah: do they perform Tamattu'? He said: 'There is no Tamattu' for them.' I said: 'And the one who resides in it?' He said: 'When he stays in it for a year or two years, he does as the people of Makkah do.' I said: 'And if he stays for a month?' He said: 'He performs Tamattu'.' I said: 'From where?' He said: 'He exits from the Haram.' I said: 'Where does he begin with the Hajj?' He said: 'From Makkah, in the manner that the people say.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ: People of Makkah / Residents of Makkah
key_terms.سَنَةً أَوْ سَنَتَيْنِ: A year or two years (duration for specific ruling)
key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعُونَ: Do they perform Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.يُهِلُّ بِالْحَجِّ: He begins with the Hajj (enters Ihram for Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Hajj for residents of Makkah depending on their duration of stay?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific ruling for residents of Makkah (Ahl al-Haram), distinguishing between long-term residents who lose the privilege of Tamattu' after one to two years and short-term residents who retain it. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that short-term residents must exit the sacred boundary (Haram) to perform their Umrah and then re-enter to perform Hajj, a practice that aligns with the general understanding of the people but is rooted in the distinct legal status of the city's inhabitants.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Dawood, from Hammad who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the people of Makkah, should they be performing Tamatto?’ Heasws said: ‘Tamatto is not for them’. I said, ‘So the residents in it?’ Heasws said: ‘When one stays for a year in it, or two years, he should do what the people of Makkah do’. I said, ‘Supposing one remains there for a month?’ Heasws said: ‘He should perform Tamatto’. I said, ‘From where?’ Heasws said: ‘He should come out from the ‘الْحَرَمِ’ Harram’. I said, ‘Where should he begin with the Hajj?’ Heasws said: ‘From Makkah, around where from what the people are saying it is (Makkah)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Dawud from Hammad who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the people of Makkah if they can perform al- Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not permissible for them to perform al- Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous).’ I then asked if a resident could perform al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous). He (the Imam) said, ‘If one resides there for one or two years he is considered as people of Makkah.’ I then asked if one who stays there for one month can he perform al-Hajj al- Tamattu‘ (advantageous)? He (the Imam) said, ‘He must perform al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous).’ I then asked, ‘Wherefrom must he commence his al-Hajj?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He must go out of al-Haram (the sacred area).’ I then asked, ‘Where must he say Talbiyah for al-Hajj?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He must say Talbiyah from where people say it.’”
